steps.prompt: These two signs differ by one tiny mark. What does each one mean?
steps.reveal: In the first, the bikes belong to several girls (girls’). In the second, all the bikes belong to one girl (girl’s). One apostrophe changes who owns what!

cards.title: Making plurals
cards.body: Most nouns add -s: dog → dogs. Words ending in s, x, z, ch or sh add -es: box → boxes, bench → benches. Consonant + y: change y to -ies: city → cities. Vowel + y: just add -s: monkey → monkeys. Many words ending in f or fe change to -ves: leaf → leaves, knife → knives.

cards.title: Irregular plurals
cards.text: child → children · man → men · woman → women · person → people · mouse → mice · tooth → teeth · foot → feet · goose → geese · sheep → sheep · deer → deer · fish → fish
cards.note: These don’t follow the rules, so learn them by heart.

cards.title: Possessives show belonging
cards.body: One owner: add ’s → the dog’s bowl, Sam’s jacket. Plural owners ending in s: add just ’ → the dogs’ bowls, the players’ locker room. Plurals that don’t end in s: add ’s → the children’s toys, the men’s team.

cards.title: Plural or possessive?
cards.telling: Banana’s for sale. The cookie’s are ready.
cards.showing: Bananas for sale. The cookies are ready. The cookie’s icing is pink.
cards.note: An apostrophe never makes a plural. Ask: does something belong to it? If not, no apostrophe.

prompts: Explain the difference between “the student’s ideas” and “the students’ ideas” in your own words.
Which plural rule or irregular plural do you most need to remember?
